correctness.rationale: Eliminating the recovery variable gives a scalar Liénard equation with damping coefficient \(\varepsilon b-f' (v)\). For \(f(v)=v-v^3/3\), the state energy \(\mathcal E=\dot v^2/2+\varepsilon U(v)\) has exact derivative \((1-\varepsilon b-v^2)\dot v^2\). Invariance of a compactly supported measure therefore gives the displayed zero balance. If \(\dot v=0\) almost surely, invariance forces equilibrium support, so a non-equilibrium measure has positive speed energy and can be normalized to the speed-weighted probability measure. At \(\varepsilon b=1\), the identity forces \(d(v^2)/dt=0\) on support trajectories and again equilibrium support; for larger products non-equilibrium recurrence is impossible. The packaged exact checker verifies the state-energy derivative and residual algebra.

value.rationale: The FitzHugh–Nagumo model is a canonical planar excitable oscillator whose local transition to firing is organized by the Jacobian trace and cubic-nullcline slope. The accepted identity shows that exactly the same trace coefficient is globally calibrated by voltage-speed energy on every compact recurrent statistical state. It yields a parameter-only weighted RMS voltage, the sharp necessary condition \(\varepsilon b<1\) for non-equilibrium compact recurrence, and a finite-amplitude crossing statement for every nonconstant cycle. This links local Hopf geometry to arbitrary stationary recurrent dynamics rather than merely recomputing a known equilibrium condition.
